clue.text: Ensuring the grenade will go off in the art studio?

definitions.text: Ensuring the grenade will go off in the art studio?

parts.words: Ensuring the grenade will go off in the art studio?
parts.note: pulling out a grenade's pin sets it off; in a studio where artists sketch, the pin used for pinning up paper is the one in question

explanation.surface: A soldier primes a grenade in the middle of an art class.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the phrase as 'drawing' (pulling out) a pin, which is what arms a grenade; in an art studio the pin is the kind that holds paper to a board.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbtack used to fix paper to a board, the stationery of a draughtsman.

clue.text: Possibly digs up a lot of untilled ground

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a moor is a stretch of open uncultivated upland

explanation.surface: A gardener digs over a large patch of wild land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly digs' is the definition by example: digs are lodgings, a rented space. 'up' turns MOOR around.
explanation.definitionFit: Digs, British slang for lodgings, are one example of a rented chamber, so 'possibly' flags the example.

clue.text: Bad candles are

definitions.meaning: a candle has a wick, so candles are furnished with wicks

explanation.definitionFit: Bad means evil or sinful; candles are, punningly, equipped with wicks.

clue.text: The usual answer given by the French

parts.note: the norm is the usual standard

explanation.surface: A typical reply comes from French speakers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is fair historically: the people who invaded England in 1066 came from a region of France.
explanation.definitionFit: The conquerors of 1066 came from Normandy in northern France, so they were French people.

clue.text: I beg you", the victim said

indicators.note: what the clue says is spoken, so a word that sounds the same is entered

parts.note: prey is the victim of a predator

explanation.surface: A captive pleads for mercy with the attacker.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned polite interjection asking please, as in 'pray, be seated'.

clue.text: Thoroughly bewilder, which is no advantage

parts.note: non is Latin and French for no
a plus is an advantage or benefit

explanation.surface: Confusing someone completely brings no benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: To perplex someone so much that they cannot think what to do.

clue.text: Nice as can be, brings tea in that's sweet

indicators.note: the tea word is put inside the rearranged letters, as the clue says brings it in
the letters of the words before could be rearranged, so they form a different order

parts.note: char is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A pleasant hostess brings in tea and it's sugary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' shuffles NICE AS into SAC INE, and 'in' puts CHAR (British slang for tea) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Saccharine describes something excessively sugary, literally or in manner.

clue.text: Remember to complain about the fractious marine

indicators.note: the moaning word goes around the rearranged letters

parts.note: bind is British slang for to moan or grumble

indicators.note: unruly, so the letters of the next word are unruly and rearranged

explanation.surface: Be sure to grumble about the bad-tempered soldier from the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fractious' shuffles MARINE into EARINM, and 'about' puts BIND (British slang for moan) around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something in mind, not forget it, is to recall or retain it.

clue.text: Told that it's not good to point

parts.note: bad means not good
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone is told that pointing is rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Bade is the past tense of bid, meaning ordered or commanded.

clue.text: Definitely make one take the wrong train

parts.note: to make someone do something is to force them

indicators.note: the letters of the next word are put the wrong way, rearranged

explanation.surface: A passenger is bullied into boarding the wrong service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' shuffles TRAIN into RTAIN after FORCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverbial phrase meaning surely, without doubt.

clue.text: Prince got lacerated by a claw

indicators.note: torn up, so the letters of the royal word are torn up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A royal is scratched by an animal's claw.
explanation.definitionFit: A crab or lobster's grasping claw has this name.

clue.text: Tries on, first, the usual excuses

indicators.note: the usual word comes before the trying-on word

parts.note: par is the normal or usual level
to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: Someone trying on clothes makes the usual excuses first.
explanation.definitionFit: Excuses as a verb means forgives, which is what a pardon does.

clue.text: Was it a cat I saw for one!

definitions.text: Was it a cat I saw for one!

parts.words: Was it a cat I saw for one!
parts.note: the quoted question reads the same letter for letter in both directions, an example of that kind of phrase

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they glimpsed a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A word or phrase reading identically forwards and backwards, like the quoted question.

clue.text: Does one chase it with a fork

definitions.text: Does one chase it with a fork

parts.words: Does one chase it with a fork
parts.note: a vegetable eaten with a fork whose name suggests something that runs, so it might need chasing

explanation.surface: A diner pursues something across the plate with cutlery.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing garden vegetable with long green pods, served at dinner.

clue.text: Saw and shot one through the heart

indicators.note: the numeral goes through the middle of the speeding word

parts.note: shot off means sped
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone witnessed a person being shot through the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Spied means caught sight of, observed.

clue.text: Its drawer opens or closes

parts.note: drawer here is the person who pulls it across, not a piece of furniture; theatre drapes are drawn open or closed

explanation.surface: A chest's drawer is either open or shut.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanging fabric screen over a window or stage, pulled to open or close.

clue.text: Steal a pill

definitions.meaning: pill is old slang for an unpleasant, tiresome person

explanation.definitionFit: To steal along is to move slowly and furtively; an obnoxious person is a slang term for a nasty type.

clue.text: Combats the spring rain and sun

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
R is the weather-map symbol for rain
S is short for sun, as in Sunday

explanation.surface: Fights against springtime showers and sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: Spars means boxes or fights in practice, so it suits combats as a verb.

clue.text: The job is a strain

definitions.meaning: one's ... of work is one's occupation
a strain is a lineage or descent

explanation.definitionFit: A line of business is an occupation; a line of descent is a family strain.

clue.text: On condition that she doubles back

indicators.note: the doubled word is then read in reverse
the condition word is written twice in a row

parts.note: if means on condition that

explanation.surface: A woman agrees only if she can retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A female name, often for a poodle, so a 'she'.

clue.text: Predestined, it is said, to be honoured

indicators.note: the phrase signals a word that sounds like the one meaning predestined

parts.note: fated means predestined

explanation.surface: Someone destined for greatness is celebrated.
explanation.definitionFit: Feted means celebrated, given a party or acclaim.

clue.text: Mineral from which the fellow has fabricated pearls

indicators.note: made up, so the letters of the next word are made into a new order

explanation.surface: A man has made a stone out of pearls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabricated' shuffles PEARLS into ELSPAR, after F for fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant spelling of feldspar, a common rock-forming mineral.

clue.text: Gentle pace unsuitable for the cat-walk?

definitions.text: Gentle pace unsuitable for the cat-walk?

parts.words: Gentle pace unsuitable for the cat-walk?
parts.note: an easy steady trot named after a canine, so not the way a feline would walk

explanation.surface: A model's slow stride would look wrong on the runway.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy jogging gait like that of a canine.

clue.text: Wanted to suppress the left, irritated by it

indicators.note: the wanting word holds down the left letter inside it

parts.note: needed means wanted

explanation.surface: A protest against the left was put down, which annoyed them.
explanation.definitionFit: Needled means provoked or annoyed.

clue.text: Mean being left to last

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
the end is the last part

explanation.surface: Someone stingy is left until last.
explanation.definitionFit: To portend is to signify or foreshadow, a sense of mean.

clue.text: Does he give money orders?

parts.note: not postal money orders but a bank cashier who gives money out to order

explanation.surface: A question about who issues postal money orders.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank cashier who pays out and receives cash.

clue.text: Otherwise buries part of the treasure

indicators.note: in another way, so the letters of the next word are arranged another way

explanation.surface: A pirate hides some of the treasure underground.
explanation.definitionFit: Precious red gemstones would be one part of a hoard.

clue.text: Go round and try to gain access

definitions.meaning: to ... a doorbell to be let in

explanation.definitionFit: To ring something is to encircle it; to ring at a door is to seek entry.

clue.text: Not a striking girl?

explanation.definitionFit: A miss is a failure to hit the target; it is also a title for a young woman.

clue.text: Right before

parts.note: a right or entitlement that takes precedence because it came earlier

explanation.surface: Something happens just ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: An earlier entitlement that takes precedence over others.

clue.text: Plan to get tight

explanation.definitionFit: To intend something is to plan it; a tightwad is stingy, miserly.

clue.text: Order suitable attire

parts.note: right means suitable or proper
dress means clothing

explanation.surface: Someone requests appropriate clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A parade-ground command telling soldiers to align with the person on their flank.
